# Generate invoices: Notion for contracts

**Pattern:** Document Generation · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers contracts work end to end across Notion, Google Drive, Google Sheets and Discord.

It moves through 29 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Receive Inbound Webhook
2. Download from Google Drive
3. Parse CSV Contents
4. Clean & Reshape Rows
5. Rows Pass Validation?
6. Quarantine Bad Rows
7. Load Rows into Notion
8. Repack as XLSX
9. Archive Processed File (Google Drive)
10. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
11. Record Sub-workflow Result
12. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
13. Archive Copy to Google Drive
14. Fingerprint for Idempotency
15. Drop Already-Processed Items
16. Load Previous Snapshot
17. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
18. Enrich with Reference Data
19. Fold In Enrichment Fields
20. Stamp Completion Time
21. Persist Run Metadata
22. Tag Pipeline Metadata
23. Align Field Names
24. Stamp Processing Time
25. Guard Non-Empty fileName
26. Save Execution Metadata
27. Summarize Run Stats
28. Append Audit Row (Notion)
29. Send Summary to Discord

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing contracts work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Receive Inbound Webhook → Download from Google Drive → Parse CSV Contents → Clean & Reshape Rows → Rows Pass Validation? → Quarantine Bad Rows → Load Rows into Notion → Repack as XLSX → Archive Processed File (Google Drive) → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Copy to Google Drive → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Align Field Names → Stamp Processing Time → Guard Non-Empty fileName → Save Execution Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Notion) → Send Summary to Discord → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Notion and Google Drive aligned by hand for contracts
- Pushing contracts events into Notion and Google Drive the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Contracts work where "Download from Google Drive" is still a manual step before Notion
- Contracts work that only reaches Notion when a webhook arrives, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Notion and Google Drive in step for contracts, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Notion or Google Drive are skipped, across all 32 nodes of this contracts build
- A failed Notion or Google Drive call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 32 nodes in this contracts build
- Every contracts run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Notion
- Fans the same result out to Google Sheets in the same run, for contracts

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Discord webhook URL; Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account; Notion integration token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Bad rows are quarantined into their own store, not dropped silently and not allowed to break the whole batch — one malformed row in a 10,000-row file shouldn't stop the other 9,999 from loading, but it also shouldn't vanish without a trace.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Feed it a file with a few deliberately malformed rows and confirm they land in quarantine, not the main store.
2. Switch the source format (e.g. csv to xlsx) and see how little actually has to change.
3. Turn on archive mode and confirm the processed file gets repacked and stored.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Drive API → OAuth2 client or Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Service Accounts have their own empty Drive — share the target folder with it.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.
_Gotcha:_ Webhook mode needs no bot token. Messages cap at 2000 characters.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.
- Google Drive: scope the credential to the one folder this workflow writes to, not `drive.readonly` across the account.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Discord: give the bot access to the destination channel only, not the whole guild.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole contracts payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your contracts process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
